paper_title: The More Popular, The Harder to Forget: Adaptive Popularity for LLM Unlearning

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Popular facts are memorised more deeply during pretraining and resist removal longer than rare ones, yet existing LLM unlearning methods apply uniform gradient pressure regardless of training-data frequency. We propose the AdaPop (Adaptive Popularity) method, which combines local token confidence with a per-fact popularity-dependent exponent derived from an external proxy (e.g., Wikidata sitelinks, LLM-as-Judge), and automates the forget-retain balance via a dual-ascent controller that adjusts the retain penalty each epoch. Across three model families and two benchmarks, AdaPop leaks ~5x less forgotten content than competing methods under paraphrased queries and ~1.6x less under adversarial reformulations. We support our analysis with internal metrics: under our method, forget-set hidden states move further from the pre-unlearning model's states than under other methods, while retain-set representations remain close.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Machine unlearning (MU) (Cao and Yang, 2015; Bourtoule et al., 2021) removes targeted knowledge from trained model without full retraining, addressing privacy, safety, and compliance risks that arise when LLMs memorise pretraining data (Carlini et al., 2021; Tirumala et al., 2022). The forget set holds the (query, answer) pairs to remove; held-out retain set measures preserved capability. Existing gradient-based and preference-learning objectives (Jang et al., 2023; Liu et al., 2022; Zhang et al., 2024; Wang et al., 2025a) treat every forget example as equally hard to erase. This assumption is empirically false: facts seen more often during pretraining are more deeply encoded and harder to remove (Kandpal et al., 2023; Merullo et al., 2025). Applying uniform gradient magnitude * a8or1suk@gmail.com 1 across the forget set therefore produces systematic failure mode, the popularity gap: rare facts are over-erased, damaging retain quality, while popular facts are under-erased and remain recoverable under paraphrase or adversarial prompts. Recent work documents this gap across methods and scales (Krishnan et al., 2025; Borisiuk et al., 2026) but proposes no training-time remedy. Yu et al. (2026) do reweight at training time, though in long-tailed image classification and from the models own predictive probability (2.3). Methods that calibrate the unlearning signal from model-intrinsic quantities (e.g., per-token confidence in Wang et al. 2025a) cannot resolve the gap, because confidence reflects current output behaviour rather than parametric encoding depth. We introduce AdaPop (Adaptive Popularity), the first training-time unlearning method to condition per-fact gradient updates on an external popularity signal (Figure 1). AdaPop converts per-fact popularity score into power-law exponent that sharpens or softens the ascent signal on each token, and pairs this reweighting with dual-ascent controller that adapts the retain penalty online. We evaluate across Llama (Grattafiori et al., 2024), Qwen (Qwen Team et al., 2025), and Gemma (Team et al., 2024) on two real-world benchmarks (Borisiuk et al., 2026; Jin et al., 2024), using MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 2021) and HellaSwag (Zellers et al., 2019) to track general capability retention. Our contributions are: Popularity-aware gradient weighting. AdaPop maps each facts external popularity (e.g., Wikidata-based proxy scores, LLM-asa-judge estimates) to per-fact power-law exponent that reweights its token-level ascent signal. This targets the popularity gap directly rather than through model confidence. Automated forget-retain balance. An epochlevel dual-ascent controller treats the retain Figure 1: Overview of AdaPop. The popularity score reweights per-fact token contributions to the forget loss; the dual-ascent controller adjusts the retain penalty each epoch to maintain retain quality (Algorithm 1). penalty as Lagrange multiplier, adjusting it in response to observed retain-loss drift. This eliminates per-dataset hyperparameter search and prevents retain collapse under increasing forget pressure. Empirical evaluation. Among methods that do not collapse, AdaPop attains the lowest adversarial-query scores on all three models and the best paraphrase scores on two of three. Token rankings and hidden states show that the answer is disrupted inside the model rather than only hidden at the output, while general capabilities stay within 0.05 MMLU of the pre-unlearning checkpoint. sections.title: 2.1 Machine Unlearning Methods
sections.content: Gradient-based unlearning methods fall into two families. Ascent-based methods maximise the negative log-likelihood on the forget set: Gradient Ascent (GA; Jang et al. 2023) does so without constraint and often collapses linguistic coherence (Yao et al., 2024; Zhang et al., 2024); Gradient Difference (GD; Liu et al. 2022) adds retain loss but treats every forget token uniformly (Jin et al., 2025); Weighted Gradient Ascent (WGA; Wang et al. 2025a) weights each tokens loss by the models confidence on that token, which makes every token contribute equally to the gradient. Preference-based methods such as Negative Preference Optimization (NPO; Zhang et al. 2024) push the output distribution away from the memorised response. Ascent-based methods forget aggressively but need retain regularisation; preference-based methods are gentler but converge more slowly on deeply memorised facts, trade-off 1https://github.com/Anya-wUw/open-unlearning we revisit empirically (5). None of the four draws on signal from outside the model: the unlearning pressure follows entirely from the models current output distribution, which does not reflect parametric encoding depth, limitation AdaPop directly addresses (3, Table 4). Łucki et al. (2025) observe that even inference-time interventions targeting outputs leave parametric knowledge intact.

sections.title: Unlearning
sections.content: LLM memorisation scales with training-corpus frequency (Carlini et al., 2023; Tirumala et al., 2022): Kandpal et al. (2023) show LLMs recall long-tail facts unreliably, and Merullo et al. (2025) demonstrate that frequent facts are encoded more linearly, providing mechanistic basis for why popular facts resist gradient-based removal. This asymmetry works against unlearning: verbatim memorisation impedes removal in both vision (Zhao et al., 2024) and LLM settings (Barbulescu and Triantafillou, 2024), and Baluta et al. (2024) show that differently exposed data points unlearn differently. Log-probabilities do not reflect memorisation depth (Wang et al., 2025a; Satvaty et al., 2024): model may assign high confidence to surface pattern even when the underlying fact is shallowly encoded. External proxies such as sitelink counts give fact-level signal independent of the models output distribution.

sections.title: 2.3 Popularity Effects on Unlearning
sections.content: Krishnan et al. (2025) show through controlled pretraining experiments that high-frequency facts are either not unlearned or only superficially forgotten, remaining extractable via adversarial queries. Borisiuk et al. (2026) establish the same failure mode on real-world facts in DUET, showing that Wikipediabased fact salience predicts unlearning difficulty across existing methods. Both works characterise 2 the popularity gap and provide the benchmarks we build on, but neither proposes training method to close it. We address this gap by introducing new adaptive popularity method (3). Local versus external calibration. Reweighting the forget signal is not itself new; what separates methods is the quantity the weight is computed from. WGA (Wang et al., 2025a) and FaLW (Yu et al., 2026) both derive it from the models own predictive probability, local signal that shifts as training proceeds. AdaPop derives its per-fact exponent from an external corpus-frequency proxy fixed before training and independent of the models outputs. The distinction is empirical rather than terminological: local weight reports what the model currently emits, so it saturates once the surface answer is suppressed, which is precisely where WGAs forget Rank turns negative while paraphrase recall survives (5.3). FaLW further requires reference distribution over unseen sameclass data; in fact-level unlearning each fact is effectively its own class, so no such distribution exists.

sections.title: 3 Adaptive Popularity Method
sections.content: We frame targeted unlearning as constrained optimisation: increase the forget-set loss while bounding retain drift. single retain coefficient α shared across all facts (GD) or confidence-based pertoken weight (WGA) cannot serve both popularity regimes: at single gradient magnitude, popular facts resist erasure while rare facts incur collateral damage (Satvaty et al., 2024; Kandpal et al., 2023). AdaPop instead combines (i) per-fact power-law exponent computed from an external popularity proxy, which reweights per-token ascent signals, and (ii) dual-ascent retain controller that updates the retain penalty each epoch.

sections.title: 4.1 Baselines
sections.content: We evaluate AdaPop against four established unlearning baselines: GA (Jang et al., 2023), GD (Liu et al., 2022), NPO (Zhang et al., 2024), and WGA (Wang et al., 2025a). Results for 11 additional methods (UNDIAL (Dong et al., 2025), RMU (Li et al., 2024), PDU (Entesari et al., 2025), NPO-SAM (Fan et al., 2025a), SimNPO (Fan et al., 2025b), SatImp (Yang et al., 2025), Adaptive 4 RMU (Dang et al., 2025), AltPO (Mekala et al., 2025), FLAT (Wang et al., 2025b), TPO (Zhou et al., 2026), and CE-U (Yang, 2025)) are in Appendix H. Main results use lr = 104, the stable operating point where most methods reach their best forgetting scores; full sweep over five learning rates is in Appendix and per-epoch dynamics in Appendix P. ROUGE-L is reported as mean std over three random seeds. AdaPop hyperparameters are in Appendix A; sensitivity to 20% perturbations of and is in Appendix C. 4.2 Models We use Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (Grattafiori et al., 2024), Gemma-7B-it (Team et al., 2024), and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (Qwen Team et al., 2025), representing the 78B scale standard in unlearning research (Zhang et al., 2024; Yao et al., 2024; Jin et al., 2024). All experiments use LoRA finetuning (Hu et al., 2022) (r=32, αLoRA=64) (Dorna et al., 2025); full fine-tuning is excluded following Borisiuk et al. (2026), who show it either fails to converge on popular facts or collapses into catastrophic forgetting. Per-model breakdowns are in Appendix L.

sections.title: 4.3 Benchmarks
sections.content: We evaluate on two real-world knowledge datasets with different popularity distributions (Figure 2): DUET (Borisiuk et al., 2026): city-centric factual QA benchmark with explicit popularity diversity. It covers broad spectrum of Wikidata scores (range: 693,763; median: 1,090), enabling direct observation of the popularity gap. We use the combined rare-and-popular forget subset with 500-sample fast retain set. We exclude RWKU (Jin et al., 2024): precision-focused benchmark testing targeted fact erasure while preserving semantically adjacent knowledge. Its popularity distribution is narrower and skewed lower (range: 0704; median: 130), suitable for evaluating erasure under lower popularity variance. benchmarks like synthetic TOFU (Maini et al., 2024), where each persona has only 20 QA samples (score range 020), too narrow to observe popularity effects. DUET provides this score natively; for RWKU we compute it from Wikidata sitelink counts following Borisiuk et al. (2026), which also tests stability across dataset-native and externally computed proxies. usable proxy need only be continuous and span roughly an order of magnitude between rare and Figure 2: Wikidata popularity-score distributions for the forget sets of DUET and RWKU. DUET spans nearly two orders of magnitude (693,763; median 1,090), providing direct test of popularity-sensitive methods; RWKU is narrower and skewed lower (median 130). popular facts (Appendix B): by Proposition 2 only the ratio of the anchors enters b, so approximate placement suffices (5.5).

sections.title: 4.4 Evaluation Metrics
sections.content: We evaluate along two dimensions: output-level behaviour and internal representation change, following established protocols (Xue et al., 2026; Shi et al., 2025). The second is essential because model may suppress correct answer at the surface while keeping the underlying fact retrievable under paraphrase or adversarial prompting, failure mode we observe with WGA (5.3). All internal metrics compare the unlearned model against the same checkpoint before unlearning; formal definitions are in Appendix J. Output-level metrics. Lower values on the forget set and higher values on the retain set indicate effective unlearning. ROUGE-L Recall (Lin, 2004): token overlap between the generated output and the gold answer. Cosine Similarity (Reimers and Gurevych, 2019): embedding-space proximity between generated and gold answer representations. model that outputs near-synonym scores low on ROUGE-L but high on cosine similarity, signal of incomplete forgetting. Internal metrics. These diagnose whether forgetting is genuine or merely surface suppression. LP: shift in the log-probability of the gold answer, summed over its tokens; large negative values on the forget set indicate the correct answer has become substantially less likely, while 5 retain-set value near zero ( 0) indicates the retained answers were left alone. Rank: change in the mean rank of the gold token in the predicted distribution; large positive values on the forget set indicate the correct answer has been demoted, stronger erasure signal than LP alone. On the retain set the value should be near zero ( 0). Hid.Cos: cosine similarity between the answertoken hidden states of the last four layers, before and after unlearning; low values on the forget set signal representational disruption beyond output suppression. KL: KL divergence between the output distributions before and after unlearning; high values on the forget set indicate parametric forgetting. Persistently high Hid.Cos, or Rank on the forget set that is near zero or negative, flags surface suppression.

sections.title: Internal Representation Analysis
sections.content: ROUGE-L and Cosine Similarity are output-level measures. We complement them with the internal metrics of 4, which probe whether the hidden representations have changed or the model has only learned to suppress surface outputs. The internal metrics separate the two leading methods more sharply than the output-level ones do: on both forget splits AdaPop has the lowest Hid.Cos and the highest Rank among stable methods, and WGAs model-averaged DUET forget Rank is negative, the opposite sign from every other method. sections.title: 6 Conclusion
sections.content: We introduced AdaPop, which derives per-fact unlearning exponent from an external popularity signal rather than from the models own confidence, and pairs it with dual-ascent controller that holds the forget-retain balance without per-dataset tuning. Across three model families and two benchmarks, AdaPop achieves the lowest adversarialquery scores among stable methods on all three models and the best paraphrase scores on two of three (5.2), with Rank and Hid.Cos indicating parametric disruption rather than surface suppression  (Table 6)  , while general capabilities stay within 0.05 MMLU of the pre-unlearning checkpoint. The finding behind those numbers is that models confidence does not reveal how deeply fact is encoded: WGA weights by confidence and suppresses only the surface answer. Any method calibrated only on what the model currently outputs inherits this failure, so closing the popularity gap needs signal from outside the model. The Wikidata score supplies one at negligible cost for entity-centric factual QA, and results are stable across proxy sources (Appendix E). Two directions follow. Popularity is one instance of more general quantity: how hard fact is to erase. Difficulty proxies for procedural, creative, or code knowledge, where sitelink counts do not apply, would carry the same mechanism into domains Wikidata cannot reach. And because βi is per-example schedule over the ascent signal, any per-fact difficulty estimate meeting the criteria of Appendix can replace it, as can criteria other than difficulty, such as harm severity or per-fact retention priority. sections.title: Limitations
sections.content: Dependency on an external popularity proxy. AdaPop requires per-sample popularity scores. The Wikidata score provides good coverage for entitycentric factual QA but is unavailable for procedural or creative knowledge. We prioritised Wikidata annotation because it is fast to compute and agrees with LLM-based labelling on 84% of binary labels (Appendix E). For domains far from entity-centric factual QA, the quality of the approximation may limit the benefit of the popularity-dependent exponent. Calibration and evaluation scope. The exponent coefficients and were derived from the DUET score distribution (Figure 2). proxy on different scale needs either rescaling to that range or recalibration through Appendix B, and Figure 3 shows the cost of doing neither: the corpusfrequency arm keeps these coefficients while spanning four orders of magnitude, which pins the exponent at βmin for most popular facts and lowers its retention. LoRA-only evaluation. All experiments use LoRA fine-tuning, following best practice in LLM unlearning research; full fine-tuning is excluded following Borisiuk et al. (2026), who show it to be less effective and to either fail to converge or induce catastrophic forgetting. LoRA and full finetuning require different optimal hyperparameter sets, and an exhaustive search for full fine-tuning is computationally expensive, so we leave that setting to future work.

sections.title: Ethics Statement
sections.content: Our data come from public sources (HuggingFace, Wikidata, Wikipedia). We do not collect sensitive attributes, and no human subjects were involved. We view machine unlearning as contribution to AI safety and data governance because it enables the removal of unsafe, outdated, or private content from deployed models. We used ChatGPT for minor language and grammatical edits; all research design, analysis, and interpretation were conducted by the authors.

Proxy requirements. For Proposition 1 to apply meaningfully across dataset, the proxy must (i) be continuous, and (ii) span at least one order of magnitude between rare and popular regions so that ln(sp/sr) in (16) produces non-degenerate exponent. Binary or coarse-threshold proxies fail because they collapse adjacent scores into single β value, even when the underlying memorisation depth differs by orders of magnitude. The Wikidata score satisfies both conditions on the benchmarks we use: DUET scores range from 69 to 3,763 (median 1,090), spanning approximately two orders of magnitude with continuous mid-tier coverage; RWKU scores range from 0 to 704 (median 130), spanning the rare-to-mid portion of the same curve. 14 Table 8: AdaPop coefficient sensitivity. Forget ROUGE-L changes by at most 0.021 across all four perturbations; retain by at most 0.041. The ranking of AdaPop relative to WGA and NPO is preserved in every configuration, confirming that the analytically derived coefficients are not narrow optimum. Mechanism. The trade-off pattern follows directly from Proposition 1. Lowering flattens the β(s) curve, increasing βi across the score range; more facts enter the self-limiting regime (βi > 1). Gradient mass concentrates on high-confidence tokens and attenuates as those tokens are erased, producing less disruptive per-step updates (retain +0.030 to +0.033 for configurations). Raising steepens the curve, pushing popular facts deeper into the near-GA regime (βi 0); under +b perturbations, the rare anchor also crosses below β = 1 (into the pressure-sustaining regime), and the dual-ascent controller absorbs the resulting retain stress. By Proposition 1 item 3, the growing effective weight amplifies both unlearning depth (F = 0.021 for a, +b) and retain pressure on the controller (R = 0.041). This is the standard forget-retain trade-off, not method instability: the (a, +b) configuration achieves the strongest forgetting and the weakest retain simultaneously, lying further along the same Pareto frontier rather than off it. The annotation protocol is described in Appendix D; here we report its downstream unlearning results, and in Appendix its agreement with the other two signals. Agreement and stability. The LLM-judge score achieves 84% agreement with the Wikidata rare/popular split on DUET, and Spearman correlation of 0.596 with it  (Table 10)  , so the two signals place nearly the same facts on each side of the split while ranking differently within side. The LLM score distribution is, however, noisier across runs and has less stable three-tier structure. Figure 3 (5.5) compares both proxies for Llama on DUET. Table 9 shows representative examples in each direction. Wikidata-rare, LLM-popular cases involve less-cited entities with distinctive attributes that the judge finds salient; model recall is more variable (0.51.0), consistent with shallower encoding. sections.title: Unlearning and the Retain Controller
sections.content: Why the ascent family. Gradient-based unlearning methods split into two families. The ascent family (GA, GD, WGA) directly maximises forgetset NLL; the preference family (NPO and variants) reframes unlearning as alignment, replacing the unbounded ascent signal with bounded preferencemargin objective. The two families exhibit opposite failure modes: ascent risks retain-set damage if not regularised, while preference-based methods converge slowly on deeply memorised facts because the KL constraint to the reference model bounds the per-step update magnitude. We adopt the ascent family because, empirically, the primary failure mode in factual unlearning is insufficient forgetting: method that preserves retain but leaves popular facts recoverable under paraphrase or adversarial prompts has not unlearned in any practical sense. Our experiments (5) confirm this: NPO maintains near-perfect retain across all settings but under-erases popular DUET facts (forget ROUGE-L 0.6260.684, recoverable under adversarial queries). Ascent is the right family because its weakness is separable from its strength. The retain-side damage can be handled by regulariser decoupled from the forget objective, which is the role of the dualascent controller. That decoupling lets AdaPop treat forget aggressiveness (via βi) and retain stability (via α) as two dedicated components instead of compromising both in single objective. The robustness evaluation  (Table 4)  provides direct empirical support. WGAs DUET paraphrase ROUGE-L exceeds AdaPops on Qwen (0.104 vs. 0.074) and Gemma (0.050 vs. 0.027), and its adversarial-attack ROUGE-L exceeds AdaPops across all three models (0.2110.396 vs. 0.144 0.262). The gap is largest on adversarial reformulations, which probe parametric encoding rather than surface output, consistent with the view that confidence-based weighting suppresses tokens the model currently outputs but leaves the underlying encoding largely intact, whereas popularity-based weighting targets the encoding itself. M.1 Dynamic Retain Coefficient as Constrained Optimisation GD and WGA use fixed retain coefficient α that must be tuned per (dataset, model) pair: too small and retain quality degrades, too large and wellmemorised popular facts survive erasure (Jin et al., 2025). The principled formulation is to treat the retain term as an inequality constraint rather than fixed penalty: min θ Lf (θ) s.t. Lr(θ) Lr(θ0) ε, (29) where θ0 is the pre-unlearning reference checkpoint and Lr is the retain loss. The Lagrangian is L(θ, λ) = Lf (θ) + λ (Lr(θ) Lr(θ0) ε) , λ 0. (30) Entesari et al. (2025) adopt the same constrained formulation for LLM unlearning. AdaPops implementation differs in two practical respects: 1. Epoch-level dual updates. λ is updated once per epoch (not per step), reducing oscillation from noisy per-batch retain losses. The drift signal δk is computed as relative deviation from the epoch-1 retain loss Rref = R1 rather than from the initial checkpoint, to absorb the unavoidable first-epoch shift from LoRA finetuning: (cid:18) δk = max 0, Rk Rref max(Rref , ξ) (cid:19) , (31) λk+1 = Π[0,λmax](λk + ηλ(δk ε)) . (32) 2. Popularity-weighted forget objective. The controller is applied to the popularityweighted forget loss Lf (Eq. 6), rather than unweighted NLL ascent. This composition lets the two components address distinct empirical failure modes, verified in Appendix N. Stability under non-convexity. Standard primaldual ascent has well-understood convergence behaviour only on convex programs. The LLM training objective is non-convex, so we do not claim formal convergence; the controller is designed for empirical stability instead. Three design choices mitigate the typical risks (limit cycles, divergence under aggressive ηλ): (i) λ updates at epoch rather than batch granularity, so δk averages over many gradient steps; (ii) λ is clipped to [0, λmax] with 21 λmax = 5.0; (iii) λ0 = 0, so the effective retain weight is α0 = 0.5 at initialisation, matching standard WGA-style retain penalty. Across the full 32 (model, benchmark) grid and the learningrate sweep in Appendix O, the controller keeps δk ε = 0.1 at every epoch, and retain-split LP and Hid.Cos for AdaPop match WGA  (Table 6)  . Empirical decoupling of the two components. The popularity exponent and the retain controller act on distinct aspects of the gradient: β reshapes the per-token weighting within the forget set (via (13)), while α scales the retain term relative to the forget term in the combined update θk+1 θk = ηθ (Lβ +αLr). They are not strictly orthogonal in the linear-algebra sense (β affects the overall forget-gradient scale as well as its direction), but they address empirically distinct failure modes: removing the controller breaks retain stability under increasing forget pressure (a magnitude problem), while flattening β to constant breaks erasure of popular facts (a per-token weighting problem). The 22 ablation in Appendix verifies this decomposition: fixing either component leaves the corresponding failure mode unaddressed, and only the full configuration achieves both deep erasure and stable retention across the tested learning-rate range. Component Ablation: Dual-Ascent Controller vs. Popularity Exponent The design rationale of AdaPop (Appendix M.1) attributes two distinct empirical failure modes to two distinct components: the retain controller addresses magnitude failure (the forget gradient overwhelming fixed retain penalty), while the popularity exponent addresses per-token weighting failure (uniform pressure on all tokens regardless of memorisation depth). We test this decomposition with 22 ablation that independently varies whether α is fixed at 0.5 or dual-ascentcontrolled, and whether βi is fixed at 0.1 (the same exponent across all facts, near-GA regime) or set by the popularity power-law: α=0.5, β=0.1: fixed retain coefficient, fixed exponent (uniform across facts). α=0.5, β=dyn: fixed retain coefficient, popularity-based βi (isolates the exponent without the controller). The decomposition predicts that fixing either component leaves its failure mode unaddressed: variants without dyn-α should lose retain quality under increasing forget pressure regardless of β, and variants without dyn-β should under-erase popular facts regardless of α. Figure 5 reports paraphrase forget ROUGE-L () and retain ROUGEL () by popularity tier across learning rates on DUET. The rare-fact plots span lr [2105, 8 104]; popular-fact plots span [2104, 8103]. The order-of-magnitude gap in the learning rate required for comparable forgetting between tiers is itself direct evidence of the popularity gap: popular facts are substantially more resistant to gradientbased erasure. Controller drives retain stability. Without the controller (α=0.5), retain on rare facts drops to 0.769 at lr=2 104, while both dyn-α variants maintain 0.927. On popular facts at higher rates, fixed-α variants fall to 0.634 at lr=5 103, while at that rate the controller keeps retain above 0.72. The forget gradient eventually overwhelms any fixed retain penalty, regardless of how it is distributed across tokens by β. The popularity exponent alone does not address this failure: it only redistributes gradient mass within the forget set, 22 leaving the forget-vs-retain magnitude ratio uncontrolled. Popularity exponent improves the Pareto frontier. At the learning rates where both dyn-α variants achieve comparable forget ROUGE-L ( 0.02 on popular facts), full AdaPop (α=dyn, β=dyn) retains 0.724 versus 0.683 for the controller-only variant (α=dyn, β=0.1). The mechanism follows from Proposition 1: βi < 1 for popular facts allocates per-token effective weight pβi1 proportionally to remaining confidence, concentrating updates on tokens that still resist erasure rather than ones that have already lost confidence. This makes forgetting more targeted, allowing the controller to apply less overall retain pressure for the same erasure depth. i,t Fixed α with dynamic β has no viable operating point. α=0.5, β=dyn achieves the highest popular-paraphrase forget ROUGE-L across the entire learning-rate sweep, reaching 0.814 at lr=2 103, close to NPOs under-erased popular tier (0.854 on Llama, Table 5). For popular facts, βi 1 already produces softly distributed pertoken signal; without the controller adapting α as forget pressure increases, the retain penalty constrains the update before deep erasure is reached. This confirms that the popularity exponent and the dual-ascent controller are complementary: the exponent shapes how gradient mass is distributed across tokens, but the controller is required to let the forget loss apply enough overall pressure to overcome popular-fact memorisation. Summary. The ablation shows that each component is necessary: the controller alone (dyn-α, β = 0.1) achieves retain stability but cannot reach deep forgetting of popular facts; the exponent alone (fixed-α, β = dyn) has no viable operating point, losing retain at the learning rates that erase popular facts and under-erasing at the rates where retain holds. RMU and UNDIAL never unlearn on entity-centric QA (forget 0.87 at every epoch); both are designed for distributional/skill-based unlearning rather than fact-level erasure. Monotonic convergence (WGA). WGA is the only baseline with smooth monotonic forgetting: forget drops from 0.122 (epoch 1) to 0.020 (epoch 10) on single seed-42 trajectory while retain stays 0.945. Any epoch beyond 4 is viable operating point, motivating WGA as the primary comparison baseline. Stable monotonic convergence is rare: GA, GD, and PDU exhibit collapse or transient instability; NPO oscillates; RMU and UNDIAL never erase entity-level facts. WGA is the only baseline that improves epoch-over-epoch without retain degradation. The dual-ascent controller in AdaPop is designed to close the stability gap that GD and NPO expose: treating the retain constraint as feedback prevents both early collapse and forget-curve oscillation.
